question: Does the BPU-compiled artefact still behave like A2's INT8 ONNX?

setup.candidate: openexplorer_oe391/model_output/student_v0_j6p_quantized_model.bc (compiled in OE 3.9.1 from A2's YAML, 300x4 calibration)

reading: All ten heads stay at cosine >= 0.9997 with zero cases below 0.999, so compiling the quantised graph for nash-p did not perturb the model beyond the calibration error already measured between FP32 and INT8. This closes a gap nobody had covered: A2 reported ORT QDQ drift and A4 had not returned compile results, so the compiled artefact had never been compared against the INT8 model it came from.

claim_scope.note: X86 simulation of the compiled artefact: numerical equivalence only. Not board latency, not a J6P measurement.
